failure: Failure: This invalidates invoking cohomology vanishing on the full normalized Hilbert ultraproduct as though approximate conjugations automatically defined a representation. It does not rule out a bounded-operator submodule, another coefficient module, a corrected action, or the flexible-stability theorem.
interface: Interface: The matrices use normalized Hilbert-Schmidt norm with denominator n; the coefficient vectors are arbitrary bounded sequences in that Hilbert norm, not necessarily uniformly bounded in operator norm. The counterexample concerns the full Hilbert ultraproduct module and a specific C2 asymptotic representation.

claims.title: A normalized Hilbert ultraproduct need not inherit the group coefficient action
